quizzes.name: Backend
quizzes.description: REST APIs, Database design, HTTP status codes, and server-side logic.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code should be returned when a resource is successfully created via a POST request?
questions.explanation: 201 Created is the standard HTTP response status code for successful resource creation.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of database indexing on frequently queried columns?
options: Significantly reduces query search time from O(N) to O(log N)
questions.explanation: Indexes (like B-Trees) provide fast lookup access paths, drastically speeding up SELECT queries.

questions.question: In FastAPI, what library is used under the hood for schema validation and request serialization?
questions.explanation: FastAPI is deeply integrated with Pydantic for data parsing, type validation, and documentation.

questions.question: What does ACID stand for in relational database management systems?
questions.explanation: ACID properties ensure database transactions are processed reliably.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is idempotent according to REST conventions?
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent: multiple identical requests have the exact same effect as a single request.

quizzes.name: Cloud
quizzes.description: Containers, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud resilience.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Docker container and a Virtual Machine (VM)?
options: Containers virtualize the hardware; VMs virtualize the OS
Containers only work on Linux servers; VMs only work on Windows
Containers share the host OS kernel and are lightweight; VMs run a full guest OS
questions.explanation: Containers share the host operating system kernel, making them lightweight and fast to start.

questions.question: In a Dockerfile, which instruction specifies the command executed when the container starts?
questions.explanation: CMD provides defaults for an executing container, whereas RUN executes during image build time.

questions.question: What does CI/CD stand for in modern cloud software engineering?
questions.explanation: CI/CD automates code integration, testing, build artifacts, and deployment pipelines.

questions.question: What is horizontal scaling in cloud architecture?
options: Adding more CPU and RAM to a single existing server instance
Switching from relational SQL to non-relational NoSQL
Migrating all data to cold archival storage
Adding more server instances or containers to distribute load across a pool
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out) means adding more machine nodes or container replicas to share traffic.

questions.question: Which principle is a core pillar of the Twelve-Factor App methodology for cloud applications?
options: Rely on local state in persistent disk
Execute background processes synchronously in the main thread
questions.explanation: Twelve-Factor App rule III states: store configuration in the environment, never in versioned code.

quizzes.name: AI/ML
quizzes.description: Vector embeddings, cosine similarity, data preprocessing, and model basics.

questions.question: What does a dense vector embedding represent in modern semantic AI systems?
options: A binary tree structure for disk storage
A compressed zip archive of text
A numerical vector in continuous multi-dimensional space capturing semantic meaning
questions.explanation: Vector embeddings represent text or entities as coordinates in semantic embedding space where similar concepts cluster together.

questions.question: What metric is most commonly used to measure angular similarity between two normalized vectors?
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity calculates the cosine of the angle between two vectors, ranging from -1 to 1.

questions.question: What is 'overfitting' in machine learning?
options: When a model performs exceptionally on training data but poorly on unseen test data
When a dataset has too few rows to train an algorithm
When the model's loss function never decreases during training
When training completes faster than expected
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise and specific training details rather than generalized patterns.

questions.question: In Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), what is the primary role of the vector database?
options: To train the foundational model from scratch
To render HTML components in the frontend
To retrieve the most relevant contextual documents based on user query similarity
To manage user passwords and JWT sessions
questions.explanation: The vector database performs fast similarity retrieval to pass relevant context chunks into the LLM prompt.

questions.question: Why is demographic data (such as gender, age, college tier) stripped in blind AI matching algorithms?
options: To prevent historical bias and ensure candidates are evaluated strictly on demonstrable skills
Because vector databases cannot store text
To make API calls run faster
questions.explanation: Stripping protected attributes prevents algorithmic bias and ensures evaluation is skills-first and fair.

quizzes.name: Embedded
quizzes.description: Microcontrollers, RTOS, memory-constrained C/C++, and hardware protocols.

questions.question: Which C keyword tells the compiler that a variable (such as a hardware register) can change outside normal program flow?
questions.explanation: volatile stops the compiler from optimising away reads and writes, which is essential for memory-mapped registers and variables shared with interrupts.

questions.question: What is the main guarantee a real-time operating system (RTOS) provides?
options: Higher average throughput than any desktop OS
Deterministic task scheduling with bounded response times
questions.explanation: An RTOS is about predictability: tasks are scheduled so deadlines can be met within a known, bounded time.

questions.question: How many signal lines does the I2C bus use?
questions.explanation: I2C uses two lines: SDA (data) and SCL (clock). Many devices share them using addresses.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a watchdog timer?
options: Reset the system if the firmware stops responding
questions.explanation: Firmware must periodically 'kick' the watchdog. If it hangs and stops doing so, the watchdog resets the device.

questions.question: What is the best practice for writing an interrupt service routine (ISR)?
options: Perform long blocking I/O inside it
Print debug logs over a blocking UART
Keep it short and defer heavy work to the main loop or a task
questions.explanation: ISRs should do the minimum (set a flag, copy a byte) and return quickly so other interrupts are not delayed.

quizzes.name: Python
quizzes.description: Core data types, comprehensions, functions, and everyday Python pitfalls.

questions.question: Which of these built-in Python types is immutable?
questions.explanation: Tuples cannot be changed after creation. Lists, dicts and sets are all mutable.

questions.question: What does [x * 2 for x in range(3)] produce?
questions.explanation: range(3) yields 0, 1, 2, and each value is doubled, giving the list [0, 2, 4].

questions.question: What is the problem with def add(item, items=[]): ... ?
options: The same list object is shared across every call that uses the default
Default arguments must always be strings
The list is copied on every call, which is slow
questions.explanation: Default values are created once, when the function is defined. Use items=None and create the list inside the function.

questions.question: What does 'with open(path) as f:' guarantee?
options: The file is read into memory at once
The file is opened in binary mode
The file can never raise an error
The file is closed when the block exits, even if an exception occurs
questions.explanation: The context manager closes the file automatically on exit, including when an exception is raised.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and is?
options: == compares values, is checks whether both names refer to the same object
questions.explanation: Two different lists with the same contents are == but not 'is'. Use 'is' mainly for None checks.

quizzes.name: JavaScript
quizzes.description: Types, equality, scoping, promises, and array methods.

questions.question: What does typeof null return?
questions.explanation: This is a long-standing quirk of the language: typeof null is "object".

questions.question: How does === differ from ==?
options: === compares value and type without type coercion
questions.explanation: == converts types before comparing (so 1 == '1' is true), while === does not (1 === '1' is false).

questions.question: What is the key difference between let and var?
options: let is block-scoped, var is function-scoped
questions.explanation: A let variable exists only inside the nearest block { }, which avoids many bugs caused by var's function scope and hoisting.

questions.question: What does a Promise represent?
options: A function that always runs synchronously
The eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation
questions.explanation: A Promise is a placeholder for a future result; it settles as either fulfilled or rejected.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].map(x => x * 2) do?
options: Returns a new array [2, 4, 6] and leaves the original unchanged
Returns only the values greater than 2
questions.explanation: map creates a new array from the return value of the callback; it never mutates the source array.

quizzes.name: TypeScript
quizzes.description: Static types, interfaces, unions, and how TypeScript compiles.

questions.question: What is the main thing TypeScript adds to JavaScript?
options: Static type checking before the code runs
questions.explanation: TypeScript checks types at compile time, catching many errors before the code is executed.

questions.question: What is an interface typically used for?
options: Describing the shape of an object
questions.explanation: An interface names the properties and types an object is expected to have.

questions.question: How is the type unknown safer than any?
options: You must narrow or check an unknown value before using it
questions.explanation: any switches off type checking. unknown accepts any value but forces you to check its type before use.

questions.question: What is the type string | number called?
questions.explanation: A union type allows a value to be one of several types.

questions.question: Do TypeScript type annotations exist when the program runs?
options: Yes, they are enforced by the browser
No, they are erased when compiling to JavaScript
questions.explanation: Types are removed during compilation, so external data (such as API responses) still needs runtime validation.

quizzes.name: SQL
quizzes.description: Joins, aggregation, keys, and safe querying.

questions.question: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the groups produced by GROUP BY.

questions.question: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: Only rows that have a match in both tables
All rows from the left table
questions.explanation: Rows without a matching partner in the other table are left out of an INNER JOIN.

questions.question: What is true of a primary key?
options: It must be a text column
It uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL
A table can have many primary keys
questions.explanation: A table has one primary key (possibly made of several columns) whose values are unique and not NULL.

questions.question: What does SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' return?
options: Every column of the paid orders
The sum of all order amounts
The number of rows whose status is 'paid'
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts the rows that remain after the WHERE filter.

questions.question: What is the standard way to prevent SQL injection?
options: Running the database on a different port
questions.explanation: Parameterised queries send user input separately from the SQL text, so it can never be executed as SQL.

quizzes.name: React
quizzes.description: Components, props, state, hooks, and list rendering.

questions.question: Which hook adds local state to a function component?
questions.explanation: useState returns the current value and a setter; calling the setter re-renders the component.

questions.question: Why does React need a key prop on list items?
options: To identify which items changed, were added, or were removed
questions.explanation: Stable keys let React match old and new items so it updates only what changed.

questions.question: When does useEffect(() => { ... }, []) run?
options: Only when the component is removed
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array means the effect runs after the initial mount only (its cleanup runs on unmount).

questions.question: What is the correct way to change state?
options: Assign to the state variable directly
Call the state setter function with the new value
questions.explanation: Mutating state directly does not trigger a re-render. Always use the setter and create new objects or arrays.

questions.question: What are props?
options: Read-only inputs passed from a parent component to a child
Private variables a component can change freely
questions.explanation: A component must not modify its own props; data flows down from parent to child.

quizzes.name: Tailwind CSS
quizzes.description: Utility classes, responsive prefixes, and state variants.

questions.question: How is Tailwind CSS best described?
questions.explanation: Tailwind provides small single-purpose classes that you combine directly in your markup.

questions.question: What does the class md:flex do?
options: Applies display: flex only on mobile
Applies display: flex on every screen size
Applies display: flex from the md breakpoint and up
Hides the element on medium screens
questions.explanation: Tailwind is mobile-first: a breakpoint prefix applies the utility at that width and larger.

questions.question: What does p-4 set by default?
questions.explanation: The default spacing scale uses 0.25rem per unit, so p-4 is 1rem (16px) of padding.

questions.question: How does Tailwind keep the production CSS file small?
options: It loads styles from a CDN at runtime
It only generates the classes it finds in your source files
questions.explanation: Tailwind scans the files listed in its content configuration and emits only the utilities actually used.

questions.question: What does hover:bg-blue-600 do?
options: Applies the blue background only while the pointer is over the element
Changes the text colour on click
questions.explanation: State variants such as hover:, focus: and disabled: apply a utility only in that state.

quizzes.name: FastAPI
quizzes.description: Routing, validation, async endpoints, and dependency injection.

questions.question: Which library does FastAPI use to validate request data?
questions.explanation: Request and response models are Pydantic models, which validate and convert incoming data.

questions.question: Where does FastAPI serve its interactive Swagger documentation by default?
questions.explanation: Swagger UI is at /docs and ReDoc is at /redoc, both generated from the OpenAPI schema.

questions.question: What is the benefit of declaring an endpoint with async def?
options: It uses multiple CPU cores automatically
The server can handle other requests while this one awaits I/O
questions.explanation: While an async endpoint awaits a database or network call, the event loop is free to serve other requests.

questions.question: What is Depends() used for?
options: Dependency injection, such as shared auth or database sessions
questions.explanation: Dependencies are functions FastAPI calls for you and whose results it passes into your endpoint.

questions.question: Which status code does FastAPI return when the request body fails validation?
questions.explanation: Validation errors produce a 422 response describing which fields were invalid.

quizzes.name: REST APIs
quizzes.description: HTTP methods, status codes, and stateless API design.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is conventionally used to replace a resource completely?
questions.explanation: PUT replaces the whole resource and is idempotent; PATCH applies a partial update.

questions.question: What does a 404 status code mean?
options: The requested resource was not found
The client is not logged in
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found means the server has nothing at the requested URL.

questions.question: What does it mean for a REST API to be stateless?
options: Each request carries everything needed; the server keeps no client session between requests
questions.explanation: Statelessness makes APIs easier to scale because any server instance can handle any request.

questions.question: Which method should never change data on the server?
questions.explanation: GET is a safe method: it only reads data, so it can be cached and repeated freely.

questions.question: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
options: 401 means not authenticated; 403 means authenticated but not allowed
401 is a server error; 403 is a success
questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized asks the client to log in; 403 Forbidden means the identity is known but lacks permission.

quizzes.name: Node.js
quizzes.description: The Node runtime, event loop, and npm basics.

questions.question: What is Node.js?
options: A JavaScript runtime built on the V8 engine
questions.explanation: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser using Chrome's V8 engine.

questions.question: How does Node.js handle many concurrent connections?
options: A single-threaded event loop with non-blocking I/O
By compiling to machine code first
questions.explanation: I/O is handed off and its callback is queued, so one thread can serve many connections.

questions.question: What is package.json for?
options: Describing the project, its dependencies, and its scripts
questions.explanation: package.json lists metadata, dependency versions, and commands such as npm run build.

questions.question: What does npm install --save-dev <package> do?
questions.explanation: devDependencies are tools needed only for development and builds, such as test runners and bundlers.

questions.question: What happens if a request handler runs a long CPU-heavy synchronous loop?
options: It blocks the event loop, so all other requests wait
Node moves it to another thread automatically
Node cancels it after one second
questions.explanation: Synchronous CPU work monopolises the single thread. Move it to a worker thread or a separate service.

quizzes.name: Docker
quizzes.description: Images, containers, ports, volumes, and Dockerfiles.

questions.question: What is the difference between an image and a container?
options: An image is a read-only template; a container is a running instance of it
A container is stored in a registry; an image is not
An image runs only on Windows
questions.explanation: You build an image once and start any number of containers from it.

questions.question: Which Dockerfile instruction sets the base image?
questions.explanation: FROM names the image that your build starts from.

questions.question: What does docker run -p 8080:80 nginx do?
options: Maps container port 8080 to host port 80
Maps host port 8080 to container port 80
questions.explanation: The format is host:container, so the site is reachable at localhost:8080.

questions.question: How do you keep data after a container is removed?
questions.explanation: A container's writable layer is deleted with it; volumes live outside the container lifecycle.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of a multi-stage build?
options: A smaller final image, because build tools stay in earlier stages
It removes the need for a registry
questions.explanation: You compile in one stage and copy only the output into a slim final stage.

quizzes.name: Kubernetes
quizzes.description: Pods, Deployments, Services, and health probes.

questions.question: What is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes?
questions.explanation: A Pod wraps one or more containers that share networking and storage.

questions.question: What does a Deployment do?
options: Keeps the desired number of Pod replicas running and manages rolling updates
questions.explanation: If a Pod dies, the Deployment's ReplicaSet creates a replacement; updates roll out gradually.

questions.question: What does a Service provide?
options: A stable network endpoint for a changing set of Pods
questions.explanation: Pods come and go with new IP addresses; a Service gives them one stable name and address.

questions.question: Which command-line tool is used to talk to a cluster?
questions.explanation: kubectl sends requests to the Kubernetes API server, for example kubectl get pods.

questions.question: What happens when a Pod's readiness probe fails?
options: The Pod stops receiving traffic from Services until it passes again
questions.explanation: Readiness controls traffic. A failing liveness probe, by contrast, restarts the container.

quizzes.name: CI/CD
quizzes.description: Continuous integration, delivery, artifacts, and pipeline secrets.

questions.question: What is continuous integration?
options: Merging code frequently, with automated builds and tests on each change
Manually copying files to a server
questions.explanation: Frequent small merges verified by automation catch integration problems early.

questions.question: How does continuous deployment differ from continuous delivery?
options: Deployment releases every passing change to production automatically, with no manual approval
Deployment is only for mobile apps
questions.explanation: Continuous delivery keeps the code always releasable but a person approves the release.

questions.question: What should a pipeline do when a test fails?
options: Skip the remaining tests silently and pass
questions.explanation: A failing stage should block later stages so broken code never reaches production.

questions.question: Where should a pipeline's credentials be kept?
options: In the CI platform's encrypted secrets or a secret manager
questions.explanation: Secrets in the repository are visible to everyone with read access and stay in history forever.

questions.question: What is a build artifact?
options: The packaged output of a build, such as a container image or binary, reused by later stages
questions.explanation: Building once and promoting the same artifact ensures what was tested is what gets deployed.

quizzes.name: Linux
quizzes.description: Permissions, processes, pipes, and everyday shell commands.

questions.question: What permissions does chmod 755 file set?
options: Everyone can read, write and execute
Owner: read/write/execute; group and others: read/execute
questions.explanation: 7 = rwx for the owner, 5 = r-x for the group, 5 = r-x for others.

questions.question: Which command lists running processes?
questions.explanation: ps aux shows every process with its owner, PID, and resource usage.

questions.question: What does grep -r "error" /var/log do?
options: Searches all files under /var/log recursively for the text "error"
questions.explanation: grep prints matching lines; -r makes it descend into sub-directories.

questions.question: What does the pipe symbol | do?
options: Runs two commands at the same time independently
Sends the output of one command as the input of the next
questions.explanation: For example, ps aux | grep python filters the process list.

questions.question: Which signal does kill -9 send?
options: SIGKILL, which the process cannot catch or ignore
SIGTERM, a polite request to exit
questions.explanation: Try plain kill (SIGTERM) first so the process can clean up; use -9 only as a last resort.

quizzes.name: Git
quizzes.description: Cloning, staging, branches, and undoing changes safely.

questions.question: What does git clone do?
options: Copies a remote repository, including its history, to your machine
questions.explanation: clone downloads the full repository and sets the source as the 'origin' remote.

questions.question: What does git add do?
options: Stages changes for the next commit
questions.explanation: Only staged changes are included when you run git commit.

questions.question: What is a branch in Git?
options: A full copy of the repository in a new folder
A movable pointer to a commit
questions.explanation: Branches are cheap because they are just named pointers that move as you commit.

questions.question: What does git pull do by default?
options: Only downloads without changing your files
Fetches from the remote and merges into your current branch
questions.explanation: git pull is git fetch followed by git merge (or rebase, if configured).

questions.question: What is the safe way to undo a commit that is already pushed to a shared branch?
options: git revert, which adds a new commit that undoes it
questions.explanation: revert keeps history intact, so teammates' copies are not broken.

quizzes.name: Cloud Basics
quizzes.description: Service models, scaling, regions, and storage types.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)?
questions.explanation: IaaS gives you raw compute, storage and networking; you manage the operating system and above.

questions.question: What does pay-as-you-go pricing mean?
options: You pay a fixed yearly fee
You pay before you can sign up
You pay only for the resources you actually use
questions.explanation: Cloud usage is metered, so costs follow consumption rather than up-front hardware purchases.

questions.question: What is horizontal scaling?
options: Giving one server more CPU and memory
Adding more server instances to share the load
questions.explanation: Scaling out adds instances; scaling up (vertical) makes a single instance bigger.

questions.question: How do a region and an availability zone relate?
options: Regions exist only in one country
A region is a geographic area containing several isolated availability zones
questions.explanation: Spreading an app across zones protects it from the failure of a single data centre.

questions.question: What is object storage best suited for?
options: Files such as images, backups, and logs
questions.explanation: Object stores hold large amounts of unstructured data cheaply and durably.

quizzes.name: Cloud Security
quizzes.description: Least privilege, shared responsibility, encryption, and secrets.

questions.question: What does the principle of least privilege mean?
options: Grant only the permissions needed to do the job
Share one account across the team
questions.explanation: Limiting permissions limits the damage if an account or key is compromised.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, who secures what?
options: The customer secures the physical data centres
The provider secures the underlying infrastructure; the customer secures their data and configuration
questions.explanation: Misconfigured storage or access rules are the customer's responsibility, not the provider's.

questions.question: What does multi-factor authentication add?
options: A second proof of identity in addition to the password
questions.explanation: A stolen password alone is not enough when a second factor is required.

questions.question: What protects data while it travels between a browser and a server?
questions.explanation: TLS provides encryption in transit; encryption at rest protects stored data.

questions.question: Where should API keys be kept?
options: In a secret manager or environment variables, never committed to code
questions.explanation: Keys committed to a repository are easily leaked and remain in the history.

quizzes.name: Machine Learning
quizzes.description: Supervised learning, overfitting, evaluation, and metrics.

questions.question: What kind of data does supervised learning need?
questions.explanation: The model learns a mapping from inputs to the provided labels.

questions.question: What is overfitting?
options: The model is too small to learn anything
The model does well on training data but poorly on new data
The dataset has too many rows
questions.explanation: An overfitted model has memorised noise in the training set instead of general patterns.

questions.question: Why is data split into training and test sets?
options: To estimate how the model performs on data it has not seen
questions.explanation: Evaluating on the training data gives an over-optimistic picture.

questions.question: Predicting whether an email is spam or not spam is an example of:
questions.explanation: Classification predicts a category; regression predicts a continuous number.

questions.question: What does precision measure?
options: Of the items predicted positive, the share that really are positive
Of all real positives, the share that were found
questions.explanation: The second option describes recall. Precision is about how trustworthy the positive predictions are.

quizzes.name: Vector Search
quizzes.description: Embeddings, similarity measures, ANN indexes, and RAG.

questions.question: What is an embedding?
options: A list of numbers that captures the meaning of a piece of content
questions.explanation: Content with similar meaning is mapped to vectors that are close together.

questions.question: What is the cosine similarity of two vectors pointing in exactly the same direction?
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity measures the angle only: 1 for the same direction, 0 for perpendicular, -1 for opposite.

questions.question: Why use an approximate nearest neighbour (ANN) index such as HNSW?
options: To search much faster by accepting a small loss of accuracy
To reduce the number of dimensions to one
questions.explanation: Comparing a query with every stored vector is too slow at scale; ANN indexes avoid that.

questions.question: What does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) do?
options: Trains a new model from scratch for each question
Removes the need for a language model
Retrieves relevant documents and gives them to the language model as context
questions.explanation: Grounding the model in retrieved documents improves accuracy and lets it use private or recent data.

questions.question: Why must queries and documents be embedded with the same model?
options: Vectors from different models live in different spaces and cannot be compared meaningfully
questions.explanation: Each model defines its own vector space and dimensions; distances across models are meaningless.

quizzes.name: SAP BTP
quizzes.description: BTP, the CAP model, CDS, and SAP's AI and automation services.

questions.question: What does BTP stand for?
questions.explanation: SAP BTP brings together application development, data, analytics, integration and AI services.

questions.question: What is CAP in the SAP ecosystem?
options: The Cloud Application Programming Model, a framework for services in Node.js or Java
questions.explanation: CAP provides languages, libraries and tools for building enterprise services and applications.

questions.question: In CAP, what is CDS mainly used for?
questions.explanation: Core Data Services (CDS) is the modelling language for entities and the services that expose them.

questions.question: What does the Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core provide?
options: Physical GPU hardware shipped to customers
Managed access to large language models and other foundation models
questions.explanation: It gives applications governed access to models from several providers through one service.

questions.question: What is SAP Build Process Automation used for?
options: Building workflows and automating tasks with low-code tools
questions.explanation: It combines workflow management and robotic process automation, such as approval flows.

quizzes.name: SAP HANA
quizzes.description: In-memory columnar storage and the HANA Cloud vector engine.

questions.question: What kind of database is SAP HANA primarily?
questions.explanation: HANA keeps data in memory and stores it by column, which makes analytical queries very fast.

questions.question: Why is column-oriented storage good for analytics?
options: Queries read only the columns they need, and columns compress well
It makes single-row inserts the fastest possible
It removes the need for SQL
questions.explanation: Aggregating one column over millions of rows touches far less data than reading whole rows.

questions.question: What does the SAP HANA Cloud vector engine let you do?
options: Store embeddings in a vector column and run similarity searches in SQL
questions.explanation: Embeddings are stored in REAL_VECTOR columns next to business data and queried with SQL.

questions.question: Which SQL function compares two vectors by angle in SAP HANA Cloud?
questions.explanation: COSINE_SIMILARITY returns how closely two vectors point in the same direction; L2DISTANCE is also available.

questions.question: What is DUMMY in SELECT 1 FROM DUMMY?
options: A built-in one-row table used for simple expressions and connectivity checks
A reserved word that deletes data
questions.explanation: DUMMY always exists with exactly one row, so it is handy for evaluating expressions.

quizzes.name: Problem Solving
quizzes.description: Complexity, stacks, queues, hashing, searching, and sorting.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining search range.

questions.question: In what order does a stack remove items?
questions.explanation: A stack is LIFO, like a pile of plates. A queue is FIFO.

questions.question: What is the average time to look up a key in a hash map?
questions.explanation: The hash of the key points directly to its bucket, so lookups are constant time on average.

questions.question: Which data structure does breadth-first search use?
questions.explanation: A queue processes nodes level by level; depth-first search uses a stack or recursion.

questions.question: Which of these sorting algorithms guarantees O(n log n) in the worst case?
questions.explanation: Quick sort is O(n log n) on average but O(n²) in the worst case; bubble and insertion sort are O(n²).
